title: K‐feldspar pIRIR dating of Pleistocene river terraces in the Avon Valley, UK: Implications for luminescence dating, climate‐driven fluvial system responses and Palaeolithic archaeology
content:
ABSTRACT

This paper presents the first K-feldspar post-infrared infrared (pIRIR) dating of river terrace deposits from the Avon valley, a major northern tributary of the palaeo-Solent. Five pIRIR samples were obtained from three altitudinally distinct terraces (T10, T7 and T5), all previously dated using quartz OSL. While earlier OSL ages plateaued at ~300–350 ka, K-feldspar pIRIR250 age estimates extend terrace chronologies beyond this limit, yielding minimum ages of 535 ± 81 ka (T10), 429 ± 55 ka (T7) and 255 ± 33 ka and 245 ± 28 ka (T5). The pIRIR ages increase systematically with terrace altitude, diverge from quartz OSL results for the higher, older terraces, and are more consistent with expected stratigraphic relationships than the OSL dates. Integration of these ages with valley morphostratigraphy links terrace formation in the Avon valley to 100 ka glacial–interglacial cycles and places the archaeologically important Woodgreen site (T7) no later than MIS 11−10. The revised chrono-geomorphological framework allows improved correlation of Avon terraces with sequences across the Solent region, promotes the use of paired OSL-pIRIR dating to elucidate localised maximum age limits for OSL and increase the reliability of mid-Pleistocene age estimates, and provides new age constraints for Pleistocene landscape evolution and hominin activity at the north-western margin of Europe.
